formattedAddress: 110, Taiwan, Taipei City, Xinyi District, Xingya Village, Songgao Rd, 11號5樓

text.text:
Urban Paradise truly lives up to its name. This bistro-style buffet offers an elevated dining experience that blends style, flavor, and atmosphere seamlessly. The space radiates good vibes—modern yet warm, making it the perfect spot for both casual gatherings and special occasions.

The food selection is outstanding, with a creative fusion of flavors that feels both familiar and refreshingly unique. Every dish I tried was delicious, beautifully plated, and thoughtfully crafted. The cocktails deserve a special mention—they are not only visually stunning but also perfectly balanced, easily some of the best I’ve had in Taipei.

Service was attentive and professional, adding to the overall polished experience without ever feeling intrusive. Urban Paradise strikes that rare balance of great food, amazing drinks, and inviting atmosphere. A must-visit if you’re in Taipei and looking for something truly memorable.

text.text: The latest buffet spot at Taipei. Lot of quality wines & beers plus cocktails. Fresh seafood and creative food combinations. Friendly & efficient staffs. Will come back again when we visit Taiwan. Just around $60USD per person.

text.text: Nice atmosphere. The food was great and the people were amazing. There’s free-flow tap beer, mocktails, juices (they taste like real fruit juice, not cordial), coffee, and fizzy drinks. Huge scallops and oysters. I recommend the Western-style soup with the crushed pastry on top. We really enjoyed it.

text.text: The food was decent. The buffet offer international and local cuisines, featuring renowned dishes from all over the world. Some dishes though did not hit the criteria. The grill and teppanyaki section was terrible, their ingredients were not fresh and tasted average, with their meats being extremely dry, as if being left out all day. The alcohol section was extensive, including numerous wine, with a bar offering cocktail and mocktail. The western section was probably the best in my opinion. The corn soup was really good. The dessert section was decent, though some cakes tasted dry. Overall, its a decent experience but I would not be back, instead I would go to sunrise buffet (旭集) for a better experience. They have better quality meats and teppanyaki section, their desserts are much better than this buffet.
